Process: Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) grown in a fed-batch bioreactor. Biomass concentration x1 and substrate (glucose) concentration x2 are measured every hour, in g/L. The operator sets the dilution rate u1 (1/h) and the substrate concentration in the feed u2 (g/L), both held constant between switches. Three experiments of 20 h with different starting biomass and input profiles. Measurement error is about 5% of the reading plus 0.01 g/L. The growth kinetics are unknown: find the rate law that explains the data.

Fitted candidates (all on the same data, 126 readings):

Candidate C9 (asprey_2000_monod_kinetics eq 17, rate law r = theta1*x2/(theta2 + x2)):
asprey_2000_monod_kinetics + asprey_2000_monod_kinetics eq 17: chi2 227.5 vs limit 148.8 (p = 0.000) (LACK OF FIT); AIC 235.5; probability 0.000
   theta1   0.2845  95% CI [0.2778, 0.2912]  t 42.64
   theta2   0.06419  95% CI [0.06012, 0.06825]  t 15.81
   theta3   0.4903  95% CI [0.4772, 0.5035]  t 37.27
   theta4   0.03556  95% CI [0.03054, 0.04058]  t 7.08
   misfit mostly in: E2:x2 (chi2 78 over 21 readings, model over-predicts on average, worst at t=5 h); E1:x2 (chi2 44 over 21 readings, model under-predicts on average, worst at t=9 h); E3:x2 (chi2 41 over 21 readings, model under-predicts on average, worst at t=19 h)

Candidate C8 (asprey_2000_contois_kinetics eq 18, rate law r = theta1*x2/(theta2*x1 + x2)):
asprey_2000_monod_kinetics + asprey_2000_contois_kinetics eq 18: chi2 103.8 vs limit 148.8 (p = 0.882) (fits within the noise); AIC 111.8; probability 1.000
   theta1   0.3029  95% CI [0.295, 0.3109]  t 38.13
   theta2   0.01097  95% CI [0.0103, 0.01164]  t 16.29
   theta3   0.547  95% CI [0.5304, 0.5637]  t 32.83
   theta4   0.04904  95% CI [0.04296, 0.05511]  t 8.07

Candidate C27 (muloiwa_2020_free_laws eq 6, rate law r = mumax*x2/(Ks + x2 + x2**2/Ki)):
asprey_2000_monod_kinetics + muloiwa_2020_free_laws eq 6: chi2 224.7 vs limit 147.7 (p = 0.000) (LACK OF FIT); AIC 234.7; probability 0.000
   Ki       167.3  95% CI [-73.56, 408.1]  t 0.69  <- not estimated precisely

Round 1 of 3. Decide. If you accept, 'chosen' is the candidate label, e.g. C9.

answer.feedback: C8 fits within the measurement noise, and all parameters are estimated precisely (t-values > 1). The strong correlation between theta1 and theta3 (0.956) is a caveat: a more informative experiment could help separate them, but it does not prevent acceptance.
answer.reasoning: C8 is the only candidate that fits within the 95% chi-square limit with every parameter precisely estimated. Its Akaike weight is 1.000; C9 and C27 show clear lack of fit, and C27 also has an imprecisely estimated parameter.
